description.narrative: The project is implemented in Zimbabwe. The main outcome areas it contributes to are countering the threats to democracy and human rights. The main rights holders are political parties in parliament, Parliament of Zimbabwe (Presiding officers, Parliamentary Committees and Staff of Parliament), Civil society organizations and staff and board members of the Zimbabwe Institute. Through institutional strengthening, facilitating the engagement of key stakeholders, research work to provide options for decision makers, facilitating networking, capacity strengthening of CSOs and capacity strengthening of Parliament, the project aims to achieve progressive development within the outcome areas.Project OrganisationsThe project is a cooperation between Zimbabwe Institute and The Palme Center. The project is implemented with the support of Akademikerfrbundet SSR, The Union for Professionals. Zimbabwe Insititute was founded in 2003 as an independent think-tank to develop developmental policies for a future Zimbabwe. ZI has developed a critical niche as a facilitator, dialogue and consensus building organization that is uncharacteristically able to work across Zimbabwes deeply polarised political parties and civic society. ZIs programming managed to engage in low-cost, high-impact interventions that are based on giving the major political players in Zimbabwe space to make consensual decisions. Its vision is the enhanced engagement of key stakeholders in building a tolerant, peaceful and democratic Zimbabwe. The Union for Professionals is a trade union for university graduates with a degree in social science, behavioral science or social work. The union organize around 70 000 members in both the public and the private sectors. The organization consists of more than 300 local and regional organizations, with one national office based in Stockholm.Other Donors to the OrganisationOther donors to this organisation is European Union and Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, PACT-Zimbabwe (USAID funding), OSISA Open Society Initiative in Southern Africa, Norwegian Peoples Aid, Netherlands Institute for Multi-party Democracy and Embassy of Switzerland. With NPA and NIMD there is collaboration, especially within the frameworks of the Zimbabwe Europe Networkwhich provides a platform to engage with EU insititutions.Project Objective1. Institutional Strengthening: The work of the Zimbabwe Institute involves senior national leadership in various sectors, this requires ZI to demonstrate gravitas for it to retain its current mandate as convener of consensus building processes. In this regard, to effectively carry out this role, there is need to ensure a strong institution with the capacity to deliver on the mandate. This entails retaining an experienced senior team with networks and skills. The senior team also needs to have a sufficiently skilled support team to ensure efficient delivery. The diverse nature and interests of the different stakeholders that are involved require a team that is commensurately equipped. Constant regular strategic planning, training and peer learning for the team is essential as they have to tackle dynamic political, social and economic situations in the nation building process. 2. Facilitating the engagement of key stakeholders ZI firmly believes that finding national solutions to the challenges facing the country requires consensus building of key stakeholders that include political parties, civil society and parliament. ZI will create safe spaces engagement and consensus building amongst the key stakeholders. 3. Research work to provide options for decision makers The various engagement platforms that ZI will facilitate will be underpinned by comprehensive research papers that will give leaders from different stakeholders the capacity to make informed decisions from the various options provided. 4. Facilitating networking Building consensus requires regular engagements within and across the stakeholders to ensure stronger potential for collaboration and consensus. ZI will work to strengthen networking as a means to contribute towards this objective. 5. Capacity strengthening of CSOs ZI will work to strengthen the capacity of CSOs in order to ensure they have the capacity to play their role of contributing to democratic processes through providing policy options while at the same time playing their 4th estate role of overseeing the work of government. 6. Capacity strengthening of Parliament Strengthening Parliament to play its key roles of oversight and law making is essential for giving life to the agreements that will come out of the consensus building processes.
